# Impacts of Extreme Weather on Power in Houston, TX

In February 2021, severe winter storms hit Texas, bringing extremely low temperatures that overwhelmed the state’s single, interconnected power grid and left millions of residents without electricity, some for several days. This analysis estimates how many homes in the Houston area lost power by comparing satellite measurements of night light intensity  before (February 7) and after (February 16) the storms. Areas where night light intensity dropped by more than 200 nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹ are treated as blackout areas, excluding locations near highways where changes in traffic could also reduce brightness, and these areas are combined with OpenStreetMap building data to identify affected homes.

## Load Libraries
```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap) 
library(stars)
```

## Read in Data
```{r}
query_road <- "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'"

query_building <- "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')"

roads <- st_read(here("data", "gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg"), query = query_road)

buildings <- st_read(here("data", "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg"), query = query_building)

tile1 <- stars::read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif")
tile2 <- stars::read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif")
tile3 <- stars::read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif")
tile4 <- stars::read_stars("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif")
```

## Transform Rasters
```{r}
# Create one raster for each day
day1 <- st_mosaic(tile1, tile2)
day2 <- st_mosaic(tile3, tile4)

if (st_crs(day1) == st_crs(day2)){
  print("Coordinate Reference Systems match")
} else {
  warning("Updating coordinate reference systems to match")
  day1 <- st_transform(day1, st_crs(day2))
}

# Create a bounding box for Houston
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
                        crs = st_crs(day1))

# Crop rasters to extent of bounding box
day1_houston <- st_crop(day1, houston_bbox)
day2_houston <- st_crop(day2, houston_bbox)
```

## Create Before and After Maps
```{r}
# Create consistent brightness limits for each map
rad_limits <- c(0, quantile(day1_houston[[1]], 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))

# Create consistent scale and legend for each map
lights_scale <- tm_scale_continuous_log1p(values = "inferno", limits = rad_limits)
lights_legend <- tm_legend(title = "Radiance\n(nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹)")

# Create map before
map_before <- tm_shape(day1_houston) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = lights_scale, col.legend = lights_legend) +
  tm_title("Houston night lights, 2021-02-07 (before storms)") +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_graticules()

# Create map after
map_after <- tm_shape(day2_houston) +
  tm_raster(col.scale = lights_scale, col.legend = lights_legend) +
  tm_title("Houston night lights, 2021-02-16 (after storms)") +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_graticules()

# Arrange maps
tmap_arrange(map_before, map_after, nrow = 1)
```

## Determine Blackout Areas
```{r}
# Create difference raster
blackout <- (day1 - day2)

# Classify blackout vs non-blackout areas
blackout[blackout <= 200] <- NA
blackout[!is.na(blackout)] <- 1

# Turn the raster into a vector
blackout_vect <- st_as_sf(blackout)
blackout_vect <- st_make_valid(blackout_vect)

# Transform vector CRS
blackout_vect_transform <- st_transform(blackout_vect, crs = "EPSG:3083")

# Crop vector to Houston extent
blackout_vect_transform_crop <- st_crop(blackout_vect_transform, houston_bbox)

# Create 200m buffer around roads
roads_buffer <- roads |>
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(blackout_vect_crop_transform)) |>
  st_buffer(dist = 200) |>
  st_union()

# Remove areas within buffer
blackout_no_hwy <- st_difference(blackout_vect_crop_transform, roads_buffer)

# Check CRS match
if (st_crs(buildings) == st_crs(blackout_no_hwy)){
  print("Coordinate reference systems match")
} else {
  warning("Updating coordinate reference systems to match")
  buildings <- st_transform(buildings, crs = st_crs(blackout_no_hwy))
}

# Keep buildings that touch a blackout area
blackout_homes <- st_filter(buildings, blackout_no_hwy, .predicate = st_intersects)

# Find number of blackout homes
n_homes <- nrow(blackout_homes)
n_homes
```

## Map Blackout Homes
```{r}
tm_shape(blackout_homes) +
  tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
  tm_polygons(fill = "firebrick", col = "firebrick", lwd = 1.5) +
  tm_add_legend(type = "polygons", labels = "Home that lost power", fill = "firebrick") +
  tm_title(paste0("Homes in Houston that lost power (n = ", n_homes, ")")) +
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_compass(position = c("right", "top")) +
  tm_graticules()

```

This analysis estimates that 157,408 homes in the Houston metropolitan area lost power following the February 2021 winter storms, based on drops in night light intensity between February 7 and February 16. Visually, the night of February 7 appears signficantly brighter than the night of February 16, indicating significant outages. However, this estimate has several limitations. The 200 nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹ threshold is a somewhat arbitrary cutoff, and the roughly 500 m resolution of the VIIRS data means every home within a blackout cell is counted as affected even if only part of that area lost power. Comparing just two single-night images also ignores other things that could have contributed to this change like cloud cover and moonlight. Additionally, excluding areas within 200 m of highways likely leaves out some homes that did lose power.
